newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-GRIFFEY HOMERS TWICE AS MARINERS BEAT WORLD CHAMPIONS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-GRIFFEY HOMERS TWICE AS MARINERS BEAT WORLD CHAMPIONS.

text.p: The World Series champion New York Yankees began their title defence Tuesday, but Ken Griffey Jr. stole their thunder by belting two home runs to lead the Seattle Mariners to a 4-2 victory on Opening Day of the 1997 baseball season.

Griffey, who hit 49 homers in 140 games last season, picked up right where he left off, homering in his first two at-bats against Yankees starter David Cone for the 22nd multiple homer game of his career.
Russ Davis also homered off Cone to lead off the third inning.

Jeff Fassero, acquired in a trade after spending six seasons with the Montreal Expos, allowed five hits over seven innings in his American League debut. He gave up a run in each of the first two innings but shut the Yankees down after that.
Cone, who missed most of last season after having an aneurysm removed from his pitching shoulder, was tagged for four runs and seven hits in six innings. He walked two and struck out eight.
In 72 innings last season, Cone surrendered just three homers. Tuesday's outing marked just the fifth time the veteran hurler has given up three homers in one game.
"Cone wasn't throwing quite as hard as I remember him," said Griffey.
"On the second one he fooled me and I only got a little piece of it," Griffey said of his third-inning blast over the right-field wall.
The Yanks scored on a sacrifice fly by Cecil Fielder in the first and a two-out RBI single by Joe Girardi in the second.
In Toronto, slugger Albert Belle began earning his monster salary almost immediately as he homered and drove in three runs in his White Sox debut to help Chicago to a 6-5 victory over the Blue Jays.
Ray Durham scored on an error by shortstop Alex Gonzalez in the top of the 10th inning to complete Chicago's opening-day comeback victory.

Belle, who left Cleveland for Chicago for a whopping $50 million, delivered an RBI double in the first and belted a two-run homer off Cy Young winner Pat Hentgen in the eighth to get the White Sox within 5-4.
Norberto Martin, who had just one homer in 140 at-bats last season, sent the game into extra innings with a pinch-hit homer off Mike Timlin to lead off the ninth.
At Minnesota, Pat Meares's two-out, two-run homer capped a four-run eighth inning as the Twins rallied for a 7-5 victory over the Detroit Tigers.
The Twins rallied from a 5-0 deficit to win for the fourth time in 11 season openers under manager Tom Kelly.
The Twins trailed 5-3 entering the eighth, but reliever Dan Miceli loaded the bases on a single by Paul Molitor and walks to Marty Cordova and Matt Lawton.
Minnesota native Terry Steinbach, who signed with the Twins as a free agent after 11 years in Oakland, singled home Molitor before Greg Colbrunn's sacrifice fly tied the game.
Meares then belted a 3-0 pitch over the centre-field fence to complete the come-from-behind win.

At Texas, Lee Stevens belted a three-run homer in the first inning and Damon Buford homered and had three RBI as the Rangers began defence of their West Division title with a 6-2 victory over the Milwaukee Brewers.
Ken Hill picked up the victory by giving up two runs, six hits and four walks with seven strikeouts over eight innings.
John Wetteland, ace closer for the Yankees last season, loaded the bases with two outs in the ninth, but got Dave Nilsson to pop out to shallow centre to preserve the win.
